method: Scope: 20 esoteric passages, 11 admitted growth evidence passages, and eight quotations in four Meta v1.1 comparison cells. Repeated quotation G03-d/G09-c is counted as two records.

Direct sequential curl HTTP retrieval, eight seconds between requests, no automatic redirects. Requested exact captures; all served timestamps come from the Archive Memento-Datetime response header, never inferred from requested URLs.

HTML text: Python HTMLParser(convert_charrefs=True), script/style removed. PDF text: pypdf 6.10.0 for Hanson and Trammell–Korinek; pdfplumber 0.11.9 for Meta because pypdf splits letters inside words. Meta quotations are checked on their cited PDF pages. The Meta Table 1 risk-threshold column is extracted separately with crop (90, 90, 245, 700) on PDF page 13 to prevent column interleaving, and checked against a rendered page. Comparison is case-sensitive NFKC plus collapsed whitespace. PDF hyphenation across line breaks is joined where necessary; original punctuation and genuine hyphens are retained. No spelling, case, quotation-mark or apostrophe folding in the reported counts.

An editorial ellipsis separates fragments that must occur in order on the same source page. The excerpt includes omitted source words. A terminal editorial ellipsis does not require a literal ellipsis in the source. This is a fragment match, not a claim that the edited quotation including ellipses is one continuous substring.

Hanson E02-01 and E05-03 required restoration of missing text-layer spaces, confirmed by machine inspection of rendered PDF pages 1 and 12. Trammell–Korinek E05-19 and E05-21 line-break hyphenation was confirmed against rendered PDF pages 56 and 4.

Machine quotation verification only; no human review, admission, classification change or evidence-check-date update. Records and packs are unchanged. Download bodies and rendered pages remain ignored; this report is the explicitly requested review artifact.

quotes.quote: Many technological enthusiasts, impressed by the potential of various envisioned technologies, have speculated that technology may soon become so productive as to induce a "singularity", a period of extremely rapid growth.
quotes.locator: Journal of Transhumanism 2 (June 1998), Wayback capture 1999-01-28; section "Introduction", para. 1
quotes.actualWording: Many technological enthusiasts, impressed by the potential of various envisioned technologies, have speculated that technology may soon become so productive as to induce a "singularity", a period of extremely rapid growth.

quotes.quote: Thus it seems unlikely that a single new technology could quickly knock the economy into a high demand mode with very high growth rates.
quotes.locator: Journal of Transhumanism 2 (June 1998), Wayback capture 1999-01-28; section "Investment Bottlenecks", final para.
quotes.actualWording: Thus it seems unlikely that a single new technology could quickly knock the economy into a high demand mode with very high growth rates.

quotes.quote: a persuasive argument for this case should explain, in standard economic terminology, why we should expect this technology to meet these conditions.
quotes.locator: Journal of Transhumanism 2 (June 1998), Wayback capture 1999-01-28; section "Conclusion", final para.
quotes.actualWording: a persuasive argument for this case should explain, in standard economic terminology, why we should expect this technology to meet these conditions.

quotes.quote: Some people interpret this as imagining a single engineer working on the task of redesigning itself to be 1% smarter. … These assumptions allow the engineer's intelligence to explode to infinity within a finite time.
quotes.locator: Robin Hanson, comment "Some Skepticism" (signed ©1998), in "Comments on Vinge's Singularity", Wayback capture 2000; para. beginning "Now let me be more critical"
quotes.actualWording: Some people interpret this as imagining a single engineer working on the task of redesigning itself to be 1% smarter. They think of intelligence as a productivity multiplier, shortening the time it takes do many mental tasks given the same other resources, and they assume this "make myself 1% smarter" task stays equally hard, as the engineer becomes smarter. These assumptions allow the engineer's intelligence to explode to infinity within a finite time.

quotes.quote: If early work focuses on the easiest improvements, however, the task of becoming more productive can get harder as the easy wins are exhausted.
quotes.locator: Robin Hanson, comment "Some Skepticism" (signed ©1998), in "Comments on Vinge's Singularity", Wayback capture 2000; para. beginning "If early work focuses"
quotes.actualWording: If early work focuses on the easiest improvements, however, the task of becoming more productive can get harder as the easy wins are exhausted.

quotes.quote: The vast economic literature on economic growth offers little support for any simple direct relation between economic growth rates and either intelligence levels or clock speeds.
quotes.locator: Robin Hanson, comment "Some Skepticism" (signed ©1998), in "Comments on Vinge's Singularity", Wayback capture 2000; para. beginning "Can we interpret Vinge's claim"
quotes.actualWording: The vast economic literature on economic growth offers little support for any simple direct relation between economic growth rates and either intelligence levels or clock speeds.

quotes.quote: within the next century we will probably begin to see a wider variety of minds, including humans who have uploaded, sped-up, and begun to explore the vast possibilities of higher bandwidths and self-modification.
quotes.locator: Robin Hanson, comment "Some Skepticism" (signed ©1998), in "Comments on Vinge's Singularity", Wayback capture 2000; para. beginning "First, let me say what I agree with"
quotes.actualWording: within the next century we will probably begin to see a wider variety of minds, including humans who have uploaded, sped-up, and begun to explore the vast possibilities of higher bandwidths and self-modification.

quotes.quote: we can understand much about quite a diverse zoo of possible minds, many of them much more capable that ourselves on many dimensions.
quotes.locator: Robin Hanson, comment "Some Skepticism" (signed ©1998), in "Comments on Vinge's Singularity", Wayback capture 2000; para. beginning "It seems to me that human cognition"
quotes.actualWording: we can understand much about quite a diverse zoo of possible minds, many of them much more capable that ourselves on many dimensions.

quotes.quote: Otherwise, we no longer have diminishing returns and steady growth solutions are no longer possible; our model predicts a continually accelerating growth rate.
quotes.locator: Hanson, "Economic Growth Given Machine Intelligence" (author-dated 1998; Wayback capture 2000-08-19), sec. 4 "Some Variations", learning-by-doing variant, p. 7
quotes.actualWording: Otherwise, we no longer have diminishing returns and steady growth solutions are no longer possible; our model predicts a continually accelerating growth rate.
